investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Cluster Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the pod never left the pending state.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 eligible nodes, and the pod's node affinity/selector rules prevent scheduling on the other 4 nodes. Because no pod was ever scheduled, the agent VM was never provisioned, and the eval runner could not collect any of the four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState). This is an infrastructure-layer scheduling failure localized to the remote-agents VM pool in the production-api environment; no evidence of a user-traffic or broader service outage is present in the packet.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:250-258: contract requires vmIdPresent=true and remoteState oneOf [running, idle, ready] — neither assertion could be evaluated because the pod never started.
possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource pool exhausted on the 2 eligible nodes: all available VM slots are occupied by existing agents or leaked/zombie VMs that were not cleaned up, leaving zero capacity for new pods.

Secondary — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: the pod spec targets only 2 of 6 nodes via affinity/selector rules; if those 2 nodes were recently cordoned, drained, or had their labels changed, effective schedulable capacity would drop to zero even if the resource quota itself was not exhausted.
Tertiary — resource quota or LimitRange at the namespace or cluster level is blocking allocation of kata.peerpods.io/vm units beyond the current count, independent of per-node capacity.

Lower confidence — a recent infrastructure change (node pool resize, node group scale-in, or VM provider quota reduction) reduced the number of kata.peerpods.io/vm units available cluster-wide before this eval ran.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Cluster Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the pod never left the pending state.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 eligible nodes, and the pod's node affinity/selector rules prevent scheduling on the other 4 nodes. Because no pod was ever scheduled, the agent VM was never provisioned, and the eval runner could not collect any of the four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState). This is an infrastructure-layer scheduling failure localized to the remote-agents VM pool in the production-api environment; no evidence of a user-traffic or broader service outage is present in the packet.
proof: failed-check.message: 'pod stuck unscheduled for 138s (Unschedulable): 0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector. preemption: 0/6 nodes are available: 2 No preemption victims found for incoming pod, 4 Preemption is not helpful for scheduling.'
failed-check.timing: latencyMs=144367, status=fail, endedAt=2026-07-04T15:59:06.933Z — pod was stuck for 138s before the eval timed out.
failed-check.evidence: evidence object is empty ({}) — no orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, or remoteState was ever written, consistent with the pod never reaching a running state.
expected-output.missing-required-evidence: all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) are absent, confirming the runner never progressed past pod scheduling.

sibling.remote-agent-runtime: identical Unschedulable message, latencyMs=149483, no evidence keys — same scheduling failure reproduced independently.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1877-1885: runner calls createAgent(args, track, 'remote', null, orgId) at line 1885, which is the call that triggers pod creation; failure at this step explains why no evidence is written downstream.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:250-258: contract requires vmIdPresent=true and remoteState oneOf [running, idle, ready] — neither assertion could be evaluated because the pod never started.
possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource pool exhausted on the 2 eligible nodes: all available VM slots are occupied by existing agents or leaked/zombie VMs that were not cleaned up, leaving zero capacity for new pods.

Secondary — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: the pod spec targets only 2 of 6 nodes via affinity/selector rules; if those 2 nodes were recently cordoned, drained, or had their labels changed, effective schedulable capacity would drop to zero even if the resource quota itself was not exhausted.
Tertiary — resource quota or LimitRange at the namespace or cluster level is blocking allocation of kata.peerpods.io/vm units beyond the current count, independent of per-node capacity.

Lower confidence — a recent infrastructure change (node pool resize, node group scale-in, or VM provider quota reduction) reduced the number of kata.peerpods.io/vm units available cluster-wide before this eval ran.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Cluster Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because every pod submitted to the Kubernetes cluster was rejected as Unschedulable: 2 nodes reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because no pod could be scheduled, no agent VM was ever provisioned, and the eval runner never received any response evidence, leaving all 5 required contract fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) absent.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that carry that label, and the other 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector requirements. This is an infrastructure-layer scheduling constraint, not an application code defect. The scheduler confirmed preemption cannot help (no preemption victims found, preemption not helpful on the remaining 4 nodes), so the pods remained Unschedulable for the full ~145 s timeout window. This is an eval-detected infrastructure availability issue scoped to the remote-agents VM provisioning path in production-api; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes: all available VM slots are occupied by existing workloads, leaving no capacity for new eval pods. This is directly stated in the scheduler message (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-create, sibling.remote-agent-state).

Secondary — node affinity/selector mismatch on 4 of 6 nodes: the pod spec requires a label or taint that only 2 nodes carry (the kata.peerpods.io/vm nodes), so the effective scheduling pool is already limited to those 2 nodes, amplifying the impact of any capacity shortfall.

Tertiary — eval probe concurrency: all three checks (remote-agent-create at ~15:57, remote-agent-state at ~15:59, remote-agent-runtime at ~16:01) ran in close succession and each attempted to provision a new VM pod, potentially competing for the same limited kata.peerpods.io/vm slots.

Lower probability — cluster node count regression: the cluster may have fewer kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes than expected (only 2 of 6 carry the resource), which could indicate a node was removed, cordoned, or failed prior to this eval run. No node-health evidence is present to confirm or deny this.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If a re-run of the eval immediately after this failure succeeds and returns all 5 required evidence fields, it would suggest the failure was transient (e.g., a briefly held lock or a pod that was just released) rather than sustained resource exhaustion.

If kubectl or the cluster API shows that kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable capacity is non-zero and no pods are currently consuming it on the 2 eligible nodes, the scheduling message would need an alternative explanation (e.g., a quota or admission webhook).

If only remote-agent-runtime failed while remote-agent-create and remote-agent-state passed in the same run window, the cause would be localized to the runtime probe rather than shared VM capacity exhaustion.

If the node affinity/selector on the pod spec was recently changed to exclude the 2 kata.peerpods.io/vm nodes, the root cause would shift from capacity exhaustion to a misconfigured pod spec — this would be visible in the pod spec diff, which is not present in the supplied evidence.
followUpEvals: Add a dedicated eval that probes kata.peerpods.io/vm node capacity directly (e.g., checks that at least N slots are available across the cluster) so scheduling headroom is monitored independently of agent creation.

Add a cluster-node-health check to the remote-agents feature that verifies the expected number of kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes are Ready, catching node loss before it causes pod scheduling failures.

Add a pending-pod-timeout eval that alerts if any remote-agent pod remains in Pending state for more than a configurable threshold (e.g., 60s), providing earlier signal than the current ~145s probe timeout.

Consider a canary eval that provisions and immediately destroys a minimal remote agent pod on a schedule shorter than the current staleAfterMinutes=20 window, so capacity exhaustion is detected faster.
